three steps to knowledge.

What makes reasoning emerge?
Archive
Submit question
1 — Hypothesize

Every project starts with a falsifiable question about how intelligence works.

2 — Experiment

We train, probe, and measure — at small scale first, then at the frontier.

3 — Publish

Results ship as papers, open models, and tools the whole field can verify.

Principles

The principles behind
everything we publish.

Rigor First

Claims earn their place through preregistered evals and replication, not demos.

Open by Default

Papers, weights, and negative results — published for the field to build on.

Safety-Weighted

Capability work is paced by our ability to evaluate and align it.

Small Teams

Researcher-led groups with full ownership from hypothesis to publication.

Compute for Ideas

Every researcher gets the resources to test an idea the week they have it.

Long Horizons

We optimize for understanding that compounds, not quarterly launches.

FAQ

Questions answered,
clarity delivered.

Everything you need to know before getting started. Can't find what you're looking for? Reach out.

We study how large models learn, reason, and fail — spanning foundation-model training, interpretability, and alignment. Everything we learn ships as papers, open models, and tools the field can verify.

We're open by default. Weights, methods, evals, and negative results are published, and our capability work is deliberately paced by our ability to evaluate and align it — understanding comes before scale.

Yes — the Academic tier is free forever: open weights, eval suites, and datasets, released under a permissive license with attribution. Most published results can be reproduced on a single node.

Training corpora are documented end-to-end, partner data never enters shared training runs, and every release includes a data statement covering provenance, consent, and known limitations.

Yes. We run rolling residencies and joint projects year-round — most collaborations start from the Partner tier or a shared workshop paper, and grow from there.

Yes. The Frontier tier covers institutions: shared compute, embedded researchers, and a co-authored agenda shaped with your team. Talk to the lab and we'll scope it together.

We hire researchers and engineers year-round, and the residency is our main door: a paid six-month program open to unconventional backgrounds. Strong open-source work counts as much as papers.
